about.title: Errors in BHL claims in UXLC change-record notes: findings and crop recipes
about.written_by: Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), at Ben Denckla's direction, by a scratch script that reran the report's generator and checked its output against the sent page.

report.title: Errors in BHL claims in UXLC change-record notes
report.prepared_by: Claude sessions in Claude Code, at Ben Denckla's direction and with his edits.

sent_files.note: A print of the HTML, made in a Chromium browser; it embeds the same ten crops.

tracked_copy.differs_from_the_sent_html: Each of the ten BHLA scan crops is replaced by a bracketed placeholder naming its BHLA page and entry, and a paragraph below the date says so. Nothing else differs.

sources.bhla_and_bhl: The BHL Appendix A reference review on MAM-private's branch codex/bhl-appendix-a-20261016, at commit 6745feaab336c1e2548e2748f712a24c82dd71bb, under masorah-books/books/bhl/appendix-a/: reference-review.model.json, reference-change-record-links.json, body-counterparts.json and pages/page-NNNN.json. Every BHLA and BHL word here is that review's transcription of the printed page.
sources.change_records: MAM-basics' in/UXLC-misc/all_changes.json, whose records the review quotes byte for byte. Record 2026.08.05-115, newer than both, is from the 2026.10.19 change list as downloaded from tanach.us on 2026-10-19 (XML SHA-256 28a8f235c9294e113610025b9aee6734eb935e1ed352c97eacb2d6fbb5c96729).
sources.generator: make_report.py, make_crops.py and live_records.py, untracked, under .novc/uxlc-bhl-claims/ in the primary forest's MAM-basics clone. On 2026-10-19 this file's builder reran make_report.py and checked that the page it wrote is byte-identical to the sent HTML.
sources.hebrew: Every Hebrew string is copied by script from those sources or from the sent page, which the generator wrote from them; none is retyped. Each keeps its source's mark order, which is not always MAM's.

fields.findings: One per row of the report's tables, in the report's order.
fields.section: The report's heading for the row's table.
fields.kind: "wrong", or "unclear" where the report calls the sentence true in spirit (the passage says verse where it means word).
fields.record: The change record: id, citation, release, its tanach.us change-list link, its index in all_changes.json as a JSON pointer (null for a record newer than that file), its reference and change texts, all its notes, and whether it has the analysis tags aBHL and aBHLA. The notes are as all_changes.json gives them, with white space collapsed; a newer record's are as its change list gives them.
fields.note_index: The 0-based index, in record.notes, of the note holding the passage.
fields.passage: The exact text of the note that the finding is about. The report shows it with white space collapsed.
fields.suggestion: The replacement the report suggests for the passage: a string, a list of paragraphs, or null where the report suggests no wording.
fields.explanation: The report's parenthetical explanation of the suggestion, or null.
fields.bhla_entry: The BHLA entry the finding rests on, as the review transcribes it: its review id (p<page>-c<column>-<number>), page, column, reference, word and any further words; for "another word of the verse", the entry the passage overlooks. Null when the finding is about the BHL body alone.
fields.words: The report's Words cell, top to bottom: each word with its label, or same_as naming the word above that it equals. UXLC's words are shown as the report shows them: an atom ending in maqaf joined to the next, and no sof pasuq.
fields.crop: For a first-table row, the entry id of its crop in crops.
fields.report_note: The first table's numbered note for the row, as plain text.
fields.untagged_bhla_agreements: Records whose resulting UXLC word is BHLA's but that lack the aBHLA tag; the report says each record's page says, by default, "The UXLC does not agree with either BHL text."
fields.scans: The BHLA page scans that the crops are cut from, as committed to MAM-private at the commit named, each identified there by path and git blob, and anywhere by byte count and SHA-256. MAM-private's source-manifest.json, at that commit, lists the same files with the same byte counts and hashes.
fields.crops: A recipe for each crop that the sent copies show, in the first table's order. scan names its file in scans. rectangle is [left, top, right, bottom), in the scan's decoded pixels, top-left origin, with no EXIF orientation applied: the convention of MAM-private's source-manifest.json. To re-cut a crop, crop the decoded scan to rectangle, convert it to 8-bit grayscale (Pillow mode L) and save it as JPEG with quality 88 and optimize=True. With Pillow 12.3.0, on 2026-10-19, that reproduced every output byte for byte. shown_at is the width and height at which the sent page showed the crop, half its pixels.
fields.crop_rectangles_chosen: Each rectangle spans the entry's column, between the midpoints of the gutters around it (60 pixels beyond an outermost column), and the height of the review's box for the entry, trimmed left and right to 24 pixels beyond the ink: pixels darker than 110 after a 3-by-3 median filter.

report_note.text: Prov 12:10.7: our transcription of BHLA has the silluq on the zayin, after its qamats, but BHLA's marks there are cramped, so that assignment is uncertain. Even so, BHLA as we transcribe it and “UXLC after” agree on the main point: both have the silluq between the qamats and the ḥiriq. What is unclear, in the manuscript as in BHLA, is whether the silluq is on the resh, before its ḥiriq, or on the zayin, after its qamats. “UXLC after” has it on the resh, which is in some ways the more charitable interpretation of the manuscript: it posits only an “early silluq”, not a change to the word's stress.

report_note.text: Job 10:15.12: on its first yod, UXLC's word after the change has three characters, in this order: HEBREW ACCENT MERKHA (U+05A5), ZERO WIDTH JOINER (U+200D) and HEBREW POINT HIRIQ (U+05B4). UXLC's joiner keeps the merkha displayed before the ḥiriq, as the record's note describes the manuscript: “a sloping line followed by a hiriq.” Side by side, the merkha's stroke and the ḥiriq's dot look like a tevir, but the word has no HEBREW ACCENT TEVIR (U+059B).

findings.section: Other errors about BHLA

notes: The qere word in the left margin, תצרנה, has the order of the tsade/resh reversed from that of the ketiv body text, תרצנה. In the ketiv body text the resh has a meteg; the tsade has a holam above the letter and a (weak) sheva below the letter. Letter by letter transposition of the markings puts a meteg on tsade and a holam above and a sheva below for the resh. Since the resh in the ketiv cannot take a dagesh, a dagesh cannot be placed in the tsade.

BHL qere word, תִּצֹּֽרְנָה׃, has a dagesh a holam on the tsade. BHLA qere word has no dagesh in the tsade, תִּצֹֽרְנָה׃; BHLA acknowledges ("instead of:") that the holam should be placed on the resh, too. The UXLC agrees with the BHLA "instead of:" qere word.

findings.passage: BHL qere word, תִּצֹּֽרְנָה׃, has a dagesh a holam on the tsade. BHLA qere word has no dagesh in the tsade, תִּצֹֽרְנָה׃; BHLA acknowledges ("instead of:") that the holam should be placed on the resh, too. The UXLC agrees with the BHLA "instead of:" qere word.
suggestion: BHLA agrees with UXLC that there is no dagesh in the צ in Leningrad.

Nonetheless, BHL body supplies, ex nihilo, a dagesh in the צ of its pointed qere, because that is the consensus pointing of this word and BHL body is merely a Leningrad-flavored consensus edition, not a diplomatic edition of Leningrad.

UXLC does not have a dagesh in the צ of its pointed qere, because UXLC is a diplomatic edition of Leningrad, albeit one that has only unpointed ketiv and pointed qere, a somewhat awkward exception to its diplomatic stance, since of course Leningrad has only pointed ketiv and unpointed qere.
BHLA agrees with UXLC that the ḥolam ḥaser dot is on the צ in Leningrad.

Nonetheless, in the journey from ketiv to qere, BHL body allows this ḥolam ḥaser dot to travel with its letter, צ, rather than stay with its letter-position, 3. Note that in BHL body and UXLC, the under-marks, silluq and sheva, stay with their letter-positions (2 and 3) rather than traveling with their letters across the רצ to צר transposition journey that is the essence of this ketiv/qere.

BHL body allows the ḥolam ḥaser dot to travel with its letter, צ, for the same reason that it supplies a dagesh in the צ of its pointed qere. BHLA notes that the consensus pointed ketiv (the "instead of" form of this word) would have the ḥolam ḥaser dot on ר.
UXLC does not allow the ḥolam ḥaser dot to travel with its letter, צ, for the same reason that its pointed qere has no dagesh in the צ.
findings.explanation: The note calls BHLA's word a qere word and writes it in the qere's letter order, תִּצֹֽרְנָה; BHLA's two words have the ketiv's letter order.

findings.section: Errors about both BHLA and the BHL body text

notes: Example from BHL "Qere and Ketiv", p. xxi, fourth of Dotan's 4 qere cases: unmarked qeres. Dotan has converted 13 LC qere/ketiv pairs in Deuteronomy 22 to ordinary words "For the sake of convenience and esthetic reasons". The words contain the ketiv letters with the qere markings as in the LC itself. This is one of the 13. The JPS Tanach(1999) preserves these qeres in all 13 cases. The above image shows a Masoretic dot referring to clear qere marking in the left margin: רה. The UXLC retains this qere/ketiv pair in fidelity to the LC.
BHL has no qere form for this word; it has the ketiv body text: הַֽנַּעַרָ֖. BHLA has no entry for this verse.

findings.section: Errors about both BHLA and the BHL body text

notes: The qere letters in the left margin, וישתחוו, end in two vavs, whereas the (ketiv) body text shown in the image ends in a single vav. A problem arises as to how to distribute the 3 vowel/accent markings (dagesh, qubuts, meteg) shown on the (ketiv) body text vav among the two vavs of the qere. The conventional assignment is to place a dagesh on each of the last two vavs, leaving the meteg on the next-to-last vav (וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃ as in the reference text and the BHLA qere). This replaces the qubuts with a dagesh acting as a shuruq dot. The same word appears as an ordinary word with a merkha accent in Gen 27:29.10. The UXLC places the qubuts on the next-to-last vav to be true to the LC image. A transcription note 'q' is added to emphasize this decision.

BHL has qere has no dagesh on the next-to-last vav and a dagesh in the last vav; the meteg is on the next-to-last vav, וְיִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֤וּ. BHLA agrees with the markings on the marked ketiv above, but has a dagesh on the last two vavs with the meteg on the next-to-last vav as in the reference text.

findings.passage: BHL has qere has no dagesh on the next-to-last vav and a dagesh in the last vav; the meteg is on the next-to-last vav, וְיִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֤וּ. BHLA agrees with the markings on the marked ketiv above, but has a dagesh on the last two vavs with the meteg on the next-to-last vav as in the reference text.
findings.suggestion: BHL's qere has no dagesh on the next-to-last vav and a dagesh in the last vav; the silluq is on the next-to-last vav, וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֽוּ. BHLA's pointed ketiv agrees with the markings on the LC's ketiv described above, but BHLA's qere word has a dagesh on both of the last two vavs with the silluq on the next-to-last vav as in the reference text.
findings.explanation: BHL's qere, in the margin, differs from the quoted word in three marks: pataḥ, not sheva, under the first vav; a dagesh in the yod; and silluq (the note's meteg), not mahapakh, on the next-to-last vav. In the second sentence, “the marked ketiv above” is the LC's ketiv as the record's first note describes it; the sentence's first half is about BHLA's pointed ketiv, and its second half is about BHLA's qere word.
